about: Narration for the NODES AI 2027 deck. Each cue is one sentence: 'text' is the caption, 'say' (when present) is what the voice speaks instead, 'frag' reveals the slide's build step with that data-fragment-index. 'pitch' is the under-one-minute video pitch for the call for speakers; its cues name the slide and build step to show. scripts/narrate-nodes-ai-deck.py turns this into audio/*.mp3 and narration.json.

cues.text: Hello NODES! I'm Matthias Buchhorn-Roth, a cloud and AI engineer in Berlin.
This talk is about a graph that knows when to say no.
Our open-source platform for the European Health Data Space received the Open Solution Award in the 2026 HL7 AI Challenge, and Neo4j sits right at its centre.
From 2029, the European Health Data Space opens health data to research across the Union. But only on four conditions.
First, a permit from a Health Data Access Body.
Second, citizens can opt out.
Third, the analysis happens inside a secure environment, and only results leave it.
And fourth, no result may ever identify a person.
An AI assistant over this data has to keep the same four rules, on every query, no matter who or what wrote it.
So we put everything into one Neo4j graph, with one layer per standard.
Layer one is the dataspace: participants, contracts and ODRL policies from the Dataspace Protocol.
cues.say: Layer one is the dataspace: participants, contracts and O D R L policies from the Dataspace Protocol.

cues.text: Layer two is the catalogue, in HealthDCAT-AP.
cues.say: Layer two is the catalogue, in Health D-CAT A P.

cues.text: Layer three holds the clinical records as HL7 FHIR resources.
cues.say: Layer three holds the clinical records as H L 7 FHIR resources.

cues.text: Layer four is the same care in OMOP, where research happens.
And layer five holds the codes: SNOMED CT, LOINC, ICD-10.
cues.say: And layer five holds the codes: SNOMED C T, LOINC, I C D 10.

cues.text: The point is the edges. A patient's condition, its SNOMED concept and the same person in OMOP are a single traversal apart.
Very little of this is ours alone.
APOC expands the neighbourhood around a match.
cues.say: Apoc expands the neighbourhood around a match.

cues.text: Graph Data Science computes FastRP embeddings. They run offline, with no API key, and for health data that is a sovereignty argument.
cues.say: Graph Data Science computes Fast R P embeddings. They run offline, with no A P I key, and for health data that is a sovereignty argument.

cues.text: Native vector indexes sit next to the data, so there is no second store to secure.
And the community's Text2Cypher and GraphRAG patterns gave our query chain its shape.
cues.say: And the community's text to Cypher and Graph RAG patterns gave our query chain its shape.

cues.text: All of it runs on the Community Edition.
Here is that chain. Cheapest and most predictable first.
A question first tries a reviewed Cypher template. That is deterministic, and it answers most real questions.
If no template fits, we search the full-text indexes.
Then GraphRAG: embed the question, search the vector index, expand two hops, and let a model rerank.
cues.say: Then Graph RAG: embed the question, search the vector index, expand two hops, and let a model re-rank.

cues.text: Only at the very end does a model write free Cypher.
Every step leaves a trace that the user can read.
Now the important part.
We do not guard the prompt. We guard the Cypher. Template, search or model, every query passes the same check before it runs.
This query returns the whole patient node. For a researcher, that is refused. So is a lookup by name, or a birth date handed back as it is.
A false refusal costs a researcher one rephrased question. A false pass names a patient.
Try it yourself on this slide.
Where does the scope for these checks come from? From the graph.
The participant holds a contract.
The contract covers a data product.
The product is governed by an ODRL policy.
cues.say: The product is governed by an O D R L policy.

cues.text: And it describes a dataset that the access body approved.
One query reads that path into the scope for every check.
When the permit expires, the next query fails. No redeploy, no config change, no prompt edit. Policy is data.
This is what the HL7 AI Challenge rewarded.
cues.say: This is what the H L 7 A I Challenge rewarded.

cues.text: In 2026, our platform received the Open Solution Award.
Look at the other winners: an MCP server for health information exchange, Notes-to-FHIR, closing the semantic gap between C-CDA and OMOP, provenance-first records. Many of these are graph problems.
cues.say: Look at the other winners: an M C P server for health information exchange, notes to FHIR, closing the semantic gap between C C D A and OMOP, provenance-first records. Many of these are graph problems.

cues.text: The 2027 challenge is coming. I would love to see the Neo4j community in it. Bring a graph.
So what can EHDS builders learn from graph people?
cues.say: So what can E H D S builders learn from graph people?

cues.text: One graph across standards beats one pipeline per standard.
Ground answers on codes, not on text.
Try the deterministic path first.
Structural embeddings keep you sovereign.
And show the trace. That is the explainability the AI Act will ask for.
cues.say: And show the trace. That is the explainability the A I Act will ask for.

cues.text: And what can graph builders learn from the EHDS?
cues.say: And what can graph builders learn from the E H D S?

cues.text: Refusing is a feature.
Policy belongs in the graph, next to the data it governs.
Who may see a person is a role decision, never a prompt.
And provenance is a node, not a log line.
Everything is open source, under Apache 2.0.
The live demo runs at ehds.mabu.red. A static simulation needs no sign-in, and the whole stack runs on a laptop with 127 synthetic patients.
cues.say: The live demo runs at e h d s dot mabu dot red. A static simulation needs no sign-in, and the whole stack runs on a laptop with a hundred and twenty-seven synthetic patients.

cues.text: Come and try to break the guardrails. Pull requests are welcome.
Thank you, and see you at NODES!

pitch.text: From 2029, Europe's Health Data Space opens health data to research, under strict rules: a permit, an opt-out, a secure environment, and no patient ever identified.
So what happens when an AI assistant answers questions over that data?
pitch.say: So what happens when an A I assistant answers questions over that data?

pitch.text: In our open-source platform, Neo4j is where the rules and the data meet: five standards, from dataspace contracts to SNOMED codes, in one graph.
GraphRAG, with embeddings that run without an API key.
pitch.say: Graph RAG, with embeddings that run without an A P I key.

pitch.text: And guardrails that check the generated Cypher, not the prompt.
It won the Open Solution Award in the 2026 HL7 AI Challenge.
pitch.say: It won the Open Solution Award in the 2026 H L 7 A I Challenge.

pitch.text: At NODES AI, I'll show you how a graph learns to say no. See you there!
pitch.say: At NODES A I, I'll show you how a graph learns to say no. See you there!
